---
title: Blocks and Signatures
aliases:
  - /guide/components/
---

A signed instruction block is a clearsigned message: the instruction stays in plain text, and a
detached signature follows it. This page walks through one real block, what each part is for, what
the signature does and does not cover, and how the extractor finds a block after a trip through a
chat client.


## A Block

The block below was produced by `sib sign` with a dev-mode key. The instruction is exactly what
Alice typed; the signature block below it is what the tool added.

```text
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNED INSTRUCTION-----
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with
scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNATURE-----
Signer: alice@example.com
Expires: 2026-09-13T22:06:30Z
Audience: acme/dev-agent

eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsImF1ZCI6ImFjbWUvZGV2LWFnZW50IiwiYjY0IjpmYWxz
ZSwiY2Fub24iOiJ0ZXh0LzEiLCJjcml0IjpbImI2NCJdLCJleHAiOiIyMDI2LTA5
LTEzVDIyOjA2OjMwWiIsImlhdCI6IjIwMjYtMDktMTNUMTQ6MDY6MzBaIiwiaXNz
IjoiYWxpY2VAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20iLCJqdGkiOiJjcGVfV2Zla0xIdkc5SC1vIiwi
a2lkIjoiYWxpY2VAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20jZGV2LTIwMjYtMDkiLCJtb2RlIjoiZGV2
IiwidHlwIjoiU0lCLzEifQ..8k1U6vxXMv7QJhNSIJbg0NsFk6C5T51ubZcoE9hZ
mgigggId48NFAhlzANHKRmIjtHJh54jYgQxgBw75lKyfAQ
-----END SIB SIGNATURE-----
```

The block has three parts:

Instruction
: Everything between `BEGIN SIB SIGNED INSTRUCTION` and `BEGIN SIB SIGNATURE`. This is the text
  the signer saw and approved, and it is the only copy of the instruction in the block. The
  verifier canonicalizes it and checks the signature over the result.

Clear metadata lines
: `Signer`, `Expires` and `Audience`, followed by a blank line. They exist so a person reading a
  file or a chat message can see who signed and until when without decoding anything. They are
  convenience copies of values in the signed header; the verifier compares them with the header
  and reports `metadata_mismatch` if someone has edited them.

Detached signature
: The base64url text up to `END SIB SIGNATURE`, wrapped at 64 columns. It is a JWS compact
  serialization with an unencoded, detached payload
  ([RFC 7515](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515) with
  [RFC 7797](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7797)), so it reads `header..signature` with an
  empty middle segment: the payload is the instruction above, not something encoded here.

Nothing in the block is opaque except the signature bytes. There is one copy of the instruction,
it is what people read, and it is what the signature covers.

::: {.callout-note}
An earlier design put the instruction inside the base64 payload with a human-readable preview
above it. That let the preview be edited while the signed text stayed hidden. Clearsigning removed
the gap. See [Design Decisions](../deep-dives/design-decisions.qmd).
:::


## The Header

The first segment of the signature decodes to a JSON object serialized with
[RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785) rules (sorted keys, no whitespace). `sib inspect`
prints it:

```json
{
  "alg": "EdDSA",
  "kid": "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09",
  "canon": "text/1",
  "iss": "alice@example.com",
  "iat": "2026-09-13T14:06:30Z",
  "exp": "2026-09-13T22:06:30Z",
  "jti": "cpe_WfekLHvG9H-o",
  "mode": "dev",
  "aud": "acme/dev-agent",
  "typ": "SIB/1",
  "b64": false,
  "crit": ["b64"]
}
```

Field names follow JOSE and JWT where a registered name exists, so a standard JWS library reads the
header unchanged. Two fields are SIB's own.

| Field | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `alg` | Signature algorithm from a closed list; `none` is never accepted. Phase 1 supports `EdDSA`. | JWS |
| `typ` | Envelope type and version, `SIB/1`. | JWS |
| `kid` | Key identifier, looked up in the [signer registry](keys.qmd). | JWS |
| `b64`, `crit` | The payload is unencoded and detached; `crit` makes `b64` mandatory to understand. | RFC 7797 |
| `canon` | The [canonicalization](canonicalization.qmd) rule applied to the instruction before signing. | SIB |
| `iss` | Issuer: the signer's stable identifier. | JWT |
| `iat`, `exp` | Issued at and expires at, RFC 3339 in UTC. | JWT |
| `jti` | Unique identifier for this block; the replay nonce. | JWT |
| `aud` | Audience: the deployment or harness that may honor the block. | JWT |
| `mode` | `dev` or `enforced`. A dev block confers nothing in enforced mode. | SIB |

`canon` is deliberately not listed in `crit`. A generic JWS library must be able to accept the
header, and canonicalization happens in the SIB layer before the bytes reach the library. The SIB
verifier itself treats an unknown `canon` value as `malformed`.


## What the Signature Covers

The signing input is the RFC 7797 form:

```text
BASE64URL(header) || "." || canonical instruction text
```

For the block above, under `text/1`, the canonical text is one line:

```text
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
```

So the signature covers:

- **Every header field**: signer, key, times, nonce, audience, mode and the canonicalization rule.
  None can be changed without invalidating the signature.

- **The instruction's words**: change one character of a word and the signature fails. Changing
  `staging` to `production` in the block above yields `invalid_signature`.

It does not cover:

- **Line structure and spacing**: under `text/1` every run of whitespace, including line breaks,
  collapses to one space before signing. A re-wrapped copy verifies. If line structure matters,
  sign with `raw/1`.

- **The clear metadata lines**: they are checked for consistency with the header, not signed
  directly. Editing them produces `metadata_mismatch`, not `invalid_signature`.

- **Anything outside the markers**: surrounding prose has no authority, whatever it says.


## Extraction

`extract()` in `sib.envelope` finds every block in a document and returns its instruction text,
its signature and its clear lines, along with byte offsets. It is tolerant on purpose, because a
block that has passed through Slack, email or a Markdown renderer rarely comes back byte for byte:

- **Dash variants**: marker lines match `-----`, `—---` and the other dash characters editors
  substitute for a run of hyphens.

- **Common prefix**: whatever precedes the dashes on the opening marker line (e.g., `> `, `# `,
  `// `) is stripped from every line of the block. A blank quoted line (`>`) is treated as blank.

- **Re-wrapping**: inside the signature segment, everything that is not a base64url character or a
  dot is discarded, so the 64-column wrapping can change freely.

- **Unterminated fragments**: a `BEGIN` without its `END` is skipped, never guessed at.

The extractor never alters the instruction text beyond prefix stripping; canonicalization is the
verifier's job. The block above, quoted with `> ` and with its markers changed to em dashes, still
verifies:

```text
--- block 1 (chars 9-767, prefix '> ')
text as written:
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with
```

Blocks are recognized only inside the markers. A file can hold several; each is verified on its own
and unsigned text between them confers no privilege.


## Inspecting a Block

`sib inspect` decodes without verifying, which is useful when a block fails and you want to see what
it claims:

```bash
sib inspect block.txt
```

```text
--- block 1 (chars 0-729, prefix '')
text as written:
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with
scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
clear lines: {"Signer": "alice@example.com", "Expires": "2026-09-13T22:06:30Z", "Audience": "acme/dev-agent"}
header: {
  "alg": "EdDSA",
  "kid": "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09",
  "canon": "text/1",
  "iss": "alice@example.com",
  "iat": "2026-09-13T14:06:30Z",
  "exp": "2026-09-13T22:06:30Z",
  "jti": "cpe_WfekLHvG9H-o",
  "mode": "dev",
  "aud": "acme/dev-agent",
  "typ": "SIB/1",
  "b64": false,
  "crit": [
    "b64"
  ]
}
signature: 8k1U6vxXMv7QJhNSIJbg0NsFk6C5T51u...
```

To check the signature, use [`sib verify`](verifier.qmd#verifying-from-the-command-line).
